llm.findings:

[RA2] expected: A reusable local token file is a form of credential persistence, but it is disclosed setup behavior rather than a hidden background session or privilege mechanism.
llm.guidance: Use a dedicated Notion integration, share only the specific pages or databases it needs, store the token in an environment variable or secret manager when possible, and if using the documented file, restrict its permissions and avoid syncing or committing it. Review POST and PATCH examples before running them because they can create or change Notion workspace content.
